reports.title: BW LPG Limited – Financial Results for Q3 2026

lines: Q4 2026 guidance • Fixed 92% of available fleet days at an average rate of ~US$102,000/day, including our fixed time charter coverage of 43% at US$44,200/day.

desk.headline: Profit to shareholders jumps to $311m (EPS $2.05) on strong VLGC rates and trading; dividend $1.30; Q4 fixed at ~$102,000/day

other.label: Product Services gross profit
other.change: vs a $24m loss a year ago

results: Profit after tax rose to $359m from $57m; profit to shareholders was $311m, or $2.05 per share basic ($2.01 diluted).
Shipping earned $84,100 per available day as spot rates more than doubled to $115,300, helped by long-haul US exports and ships avoiding the Panama Canal.
The trading arm made $146m of realised gains plus an $18m mark-to-market gain, for a $118m profit after tax.
Total revenue (shipping plus trading) was $1.13bn; operating cash flow was $328m and a $36.5m gain on ship sales also helped.
The $1.30 dividend equals 92% of shipping profit, taking the year-to-date payout to 100%; a $300m convertible bond was issued to help fund eight new ships.

guidance.summary: For Q4, 92% of available fleet days are already booked at about $102,000 a day, before accounting and hedge adjustments. For 2027, 42% of capacity is fixed on time charters at $44,000 a day.

points: CEO Kristian Sørensen said Middle East LPG exports are still far below normal; a full Strait of Hormuz reopening could narrow the US–Asia price gap and weigh on spot rates.
Panama Canal congestion and longer routes around the Cape are absorbing ship capacity.
Management prefers charters of three years or longer and wants to keep a large share of the fleet on spot.
Secondhand ship values are at record highs, and older vessels are being sold into that market.
A top-up dividend from trading profits is possible for Q4, to be decided after year-end with a trading update by mid-January.
call.source: Call transcript — The Motley Fool, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Any reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and its effect on VLGC spot rates.
